proposalDispatchEvidence.coverage: Proposal dispatch is evidence-bound (STE 4.1.2-3): the send is refused without an exact recipient, queues exactly one durable email (unique filtered index on firm+proposal) bound to the offer identity - the generated quotation artifact hash when a reviewed document exists, otherwise a deterministic digest of the reviewed proposal revision and approved quotation - and records it as SentOfferSha256. The commercial SENT status no longer claims delivery: truth is the notification's QUEUED/SENT/FAILED state with DeliveredAt, surfaced in the proposal workspace and Angular page alongside recipient and offer identity. Client acceptance must cite the exact dispatched offer hash plus a respondent name; stale, revised, or superseded offers are refused (crm.stale-offer), replay of the same response is safe, and a response citing a different offer conflicts instead of silently merging. Declines keep their mandatory reason. The mail worker discovery now covers both receipt and proposal notifications without the fee-milestone join, and pre-conversion proposal dispatches enqueue with a null client scope, which the operation store and handler explicitly accept. The receipt notification additionally binds its document hash and client for the same discovery path.

steSpecPackage1CommercialCalculation.behavior: Quotations are priced from the latest approved rate cards x hours, a complexity factor, a risk premium and a discount by a pure calculator; every recalculation is an immutable revision. A configurable approval matrix (discount bands, non-standard terms, documented Partner default) selects required approvers, blocks insufficient roles and preparers approving their own version, and gates proposal internal review. One action generates a branded Quotation and Engagement Letter (DOCX, template/profile version, SHA-256) from the approved quotation. The accepted proposal yields an agreed-fee agreement with a 50% advance and a balance; invoices follow the existing review/post path; manual advance payments handle partial, duplicate and excess amounts; a fully paid advance produces one official receipt document and one queued email delivered by the isolated mail worker; the balance invoice is issued once, only after the advance is paid and the linked engagement has an issued release. Database triggers make documents, approvals and profiles append-only and restrict agreement, milestone and quotation edits.
steSpecPackage1CommercialCalculation.boundary: Receipt email carries the receipt details in the body; the DOCX is retained on the record but not attached because the mail contract has no attachments. Provider acceptance of the email is not recipient delivery. Portal provisioning on conversion, client delegation, first-login enforcement and drag-and-drop (package 2) are not part of this slice.

fixedInThisSlice: Advance card and activation readiness now use the milestone PAID state that activation checks, not an allocation total that credit notes can inflate.
The advance is read only from a fee agreement linked to this engagement; an unlinked agreement reports NOT_LINKED, as activation refuses it.
The letter card requires the letter template, commercial profile and firm seal, in the order the letter command refuses them.
A route mismatch between the proposal and the engagement blocks the letter and reports ROUTE_MISMATCH.
Readiness requires a firm-wide grant, so an engagement-only grant cannot read client-level Partner decisions or the decider's name.
Letter and activation actions are server-computed flags (canGenerateLetter, canActivate) for the requesting actor, not inferred in the browser.
The stage 4 advance blocker is listed only while the advance is unpaid.
The engagement's proposal is the one its linked fee agreement binds, falling back to the client's newest proposal only when none is linked.
The workflow route allowlist no longer admits dot segments.

READY_FOR_REVIEW is shown as pending, not as a success state; phases carry visible status text, list semantics and canonical-order validation; 401 ends the session and 403 says the panel is unavailable to the role.
review.method: Read-only adversarial review by three independent lenses (truthfulness, authorization and exposure, Angular contract and accessibility); each finding was verified against source before action.
openDecisionsOrDeferred: The protected letter guard applies offer identity only when a dispatch record exists; the read model additionally requires the sent and response offer hashes to match. Hardening the command is an owner decision and was not changed in this slice.
FeeAgreementWorkspaceQuery.CanCreate does not repeat the quotation-revision check of the create command (pre-existing; this file is not in the slice).
With no linked fee agreement, the engagement is bound to the client's newest proposal; a newer draft for another route can hide a cleared engagement until a fee agreement is linked.
The readiness read does not pass the automatic advance-invoice setting, so the preparation message can read as drafting disabled when it is enabled.
The workflow card shows lifecycle blocker text to every role that the lifecycle endpoint already accepts; this is an existing exposure, now more prominent.
Non-permission refusals (projection and reconciliation gates) map to HTTP 403, following the existing UI read pattern.
The shared instant decoder accepts timestamps without an offset (pre-existing decoder).
No automated test drives a fully paid advance through receipt allocation; the PAID branch relies on the same milestone predicate that ActivateAsync checks, verified by code reading.
